newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends softer amid growing unrest.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends softer amid growing unrest.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 675-682 per dollar in low interbank volumes, a touch softer from the morning's 670-680 after dollar demand edged up in the afternoon amid a growing political unrest, dealers said.
"The lev eased in the afternoon because a large fuel importer was bidding for foreign currency," one dealer said.
"However, the lev's fall from Friday was mainly due to market concern over the current political instability, not to active dollar bidding," he added.

Curbs on banks' lev liquidity imposed by the central bank in December and January partly helped the lev, preventing banks from building long dollar positions in anticipation of a further lev fall, traders said.
"But the lev might slump whenever large final clients start bidding for foreign currency," another dealer said.
The central bank was not seen supporting the lev through dollar sales today, dealers said. Central bank officials were not available for comment.
About 2,000 Bulgarian students marched through Sofia on Monday delivering petitions to Western embassies urging support for the opposition's call for early general elections.

The Promyana trade union launched a series of one-hour warning strikes and the opposition planned nationwide rallies later in the day as daily protests inspired by severe economic crisis entered their second week.

Tens of thousands of Bulgarians gathered in freezing cold outside Sofia's gold-domed Alexander Nevsky cathedral on Sunday for a peaceful protest after two days of clashes in which the government said 196 people were hurt. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
